quote: We built a solar design for your home. And on my end, it says we actually never had the chance to show it to you or get you the details.
stewart_read: Rep references a prior design/appointment but never probes what happened, who was involved, or what was shown — critical since the customer immediately reveals he wasn't even present for the original call.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be intentionally keeping the call short since this is a re-book, not a full qualify — but the ambiguity about who the actual homeowner-contact was should have been resolved before locking a time.
coaching_implication: Ask 'were you the one we spoke with originally, or was that your mom?' before booking — this affects who needs to be on the appointment.

quote: Last time we spoke with you, did we end up getting a copy of your electric bill?
stewart_read: Bill question is asked purely as a checklist item after the appointment is already set, with no attempt to use it as an anchor or hook for the design conversation.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be strategically deferring detailed bill talk to the actual design appointment, since that's a natural handoff to the closer.
coaching_implication: Even a quick 'that bill is what we'll use to show your savings' framing would tie bill collection to value instead of leaving it as pure homework.

quote: I I I don't I wasn't there for that appointment. My mom must have been there. I'm not a 100% sure.
stewart_read: This reveals a likely co-owner or co-decision-maker (the mom) was the actual point of contact previously, yet the rep does not ask if the mom should be on the upcoming appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be treating William Pierre as the sole account holder deliberately, but nothing confirms that — this is a real gap.
coaching_implication: Should have asked directly: 'Is your mom on the title too? Should she join the call Friday?'

stewart_read: Rep opens with just the customer's first name and no company ID until 00:13, after the customer already had to ask 'From where?' — the legitimacy anchor came reactively, not proactively.
alternative_hypothesis: This appears to be a callback context ('Are you returning a missed call?'), which may justify a lighter intro since the customer initiated contact.
coaching_implication: Even on a callback, state company name in the first line to avoid the customer needing to ask.

quote: We just need to get some details from that. But as long as you have it ready for the appointment, we should be good.
stewart_read: Call ends without the full button-up: no restatement of the one-hour block, no no-driving/computer instruction, and no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake.
coaching_implication: Add the no-driving/computer line and a verbal fairness check before ending every booked call, regardless of call length.
